rubric_items.reason: Route auth, input allow-list, SQL binding, PAT-8 columns, logging and XSS all checked against the changed code; no missed weakness found. It does not say what the SAST scan reported (4 pre-existing results) or that none touch changed files.
Every claim and SF-1 cite the exact product line (patients.ts#L12, patientService.ts#L35, patientRepo.ts#L30/L44/L132/L150, PatientsPage.tsx#L96), and each line says what the claim states.
SF-1 is a query-cost note rated minor, which fits its impact. Open MVP permissions are rightly treated as existing state rather than raised as a new finding.
SF-1 gives a concrete fix direction: rely on the existing (patient_id, starts_at) index, or add a partial index on COMPLETED rows. That index exists in the appointments migration.
No false positives. SF-1 is openly labelled a cost note, not a vulnerability, and the correlated max() it describes really is in the shared WHERE clause.
